questions.question: What do you move with your hand to control the pointer on a computer screen?
questions.explanation: A mouse senses how it moves on the desk. The pointer on the screen moves in the same way.

questions.question: Which part of a computer do you use to type letters and numbers?
questions.explanation: A keyboard has a key for each letter and number. Many people type with all ten fingers.

questions.question: What is the screen of a desktop computer usually called?
questions.explanation: A monitor shows pictures and text from the computer. It is made of millions of tiny dots.

questions.question: What do we call a message that you send from one computer to another over the internet?
questions.explanation: Email is short for electronic mail. An email can reach someone on the other side of the world in a few seconds.

questions.question: What does the first "W" in "www" stand for?
questions.explanation: "www" means World Wide Web. It is the system of web pages that you open with a browser.

questions.question: What do we call a small program that you install on a phone?
questions.explanation: "App" is short for application. Games, maps and messaging tools are all apps.

questions.question: What do we call a person who writes instructions for computers?
questions.explanation: Programmers write code in special languages. The computer follows the code step by step.

questions.question: What do you use to look for pages on the internet by typing a few words?
questions.explanation: A search engine looks through billions of web pages and shows you the ones that fit your words.

questions.question: What do we call a robot that is built to look like a person?
questions.explanation: Humanoid robots often have a head, two arms and two legs. They can be built to walk and wave.

questions.question: What does Wi-Fi let your phone do?
questions.correct: Connect to the internet without a cable
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi sends data through the air as radio waves. A router at home or school sends and receives them.

questions.question: Which device at home sends the internet to your phone and laptop?
questions.explanation: A router shares one internet connection with many devices. Some use cables and some use Wi-Fi.

questions.question: What is a pixel?
questions.correct: A tiny dot on a screen
questions.explanation: A screen is made of many pixels, each with its own colour. Together they make pictures and words.

questions.question: In computer programs, what is a "bug"?
questions.explanation: Bugs make programs do the wrong thing. Finding and fixing them is called debugging.

questions.question: Which computer is made to be carried and has a screen that folds down?
questions.explanation: A laptop has the screen, keyboard and battery in one case. You can use it on your lap or on a table.

questions.question: Computers store everything with only two digits. Which two?
questions.explanation: This is called binary. Each 0 or 1 is one bit, and many bits together make letters, pictures and sounds.

questions.question: What do the letters "AI" stand for?
questions.explanation: Artificial intelligence means computers doing things that normally need human thinking, such as understanding speech.

questions.question: What does a 3D printer make?
questions.explanation: Many 3D printers melt plastic and build a shape layer by layer. People print toys, tools and spare parts.

questions.question: Which toy company made the Mindstorms kits for building robots that you can program?
questions.explanation: LEGO is from Billund in Denmark. In Mindstorms, children built a robot from bricks and programmed it on a computer.

questions.question: What does it mean to "download" a file?
questions.correct: To copy it from the internet
wrong: To delete it from your device
To send it to a friend
questions.explanation: When you download a song or a game, a copy is saved on your phone or computer.

questions.question: What does it mean when your computer is "online"?
questions.correct: It is connected to the internet
questions.explanation: Online means you can reach websites, send messages and play games with people far away.

questions.question: What do we call the small pictures of faces and objects that you add to text messages?
questions.explanation: The word "emoji" comes from Japanese. It means "picture character".

questions.question: What does a microphone pick up?
questions.explanation: A microphone turns sound into an electric signal. Phones, laptops and headsets all have one.

questions.question: What is the name of the stick you move with your hand to steer in many computer games?
questions.explanation: A joystick can tilt in any direction. Pilots and gamers use it to steer.

questions.question: Why should you keep your password secret?
questions.correct: So that nobody else can use your account
wrong: So that your computer runs faster
So that your battery lasts longer
So that you never forget it
questions.explanation: A strong password has many different letters, numbers and symbols. Do not use the same one everywhere.

questions.question: What is Bluetooth often used for?
wrong: To keep food fresh in a fridge
questions.explanation: Bluetooth sends data through the air over short distances, such as across a room.

questions.question: What do you do when you press "Save" on a computer?
questions.correct: Keep your work so you can open it later
questions.explanation: If you forget to save and the power goes out, your work can be lost.

questions.question: Which part of a computer is often called its brain?
questions.explanation: The processor, or CPU, follows the instructions in programs. A fast one can do billions of steps every second.

questions.question: Which British scientist invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: He invented the web in 1989 while working in Switzerland. His idea was to share information between computers.

questions.question: What does pressing the Ctrl key and the C key together usually do?
questions.correct: It copies what you have chosen
questions.explanation: Ctrl and V then pastes the copy somewhere else. These shortcuts save a lot of time.

questions.question: What does a webcam do?
questions.correct: It films video for video calls
questions.explanation: A webcam is a small camera on or near your screen. It lets friends and family see you in a video call.

questions.question: Which long key on a keyboard makes a gap between words?
questions.explanation: The space bar is the longest key on most keyboards. It is made to be hit easily with a thumb.

questions.question: Which is the best description of a robot?
questions.explanation: Robots can have sensors to see or feel. Some work in factories and some clean floors or explore.

questions.question: What do you use to look at web pages on a computer?
questions.explanation: A browser opens web pages for you. You type an address or a search into it.

questions.question: What is a PIN?
questions.explanation: PIN is short for personal identification number. A bank card PIN usually has four numbers, and you should not tell anyone.

questions.question: What is the internet?
wrong: A big computer in one building
questions.explanation: The internet joins many networks all over the world. Websites, email and video calls all travel over it.

questions.question: What do people use a USB stick for?
questions.explanation: A USB stick is small and can hold thousands of photos. You plug it into the USB port.

questions.question: What does a printer do?
questions.correct: It puts words and pictures on paper
questions.explanation: Many printers spray tiny drops of ink onto the paper. Others use a fine powder called toner.

questions.question: What do shop scanners read to find out the price of a product?
questions.explanation: A barcode is a pattern of black and white stripes. Many scanners read it with a red light.

questions.question: What can a robot lawn mower do?
questions.explanation: It drives around the garden alone and goes back to its charger when the battery is low.

questions.question: What do we call a flat computer with a touchscreen that is bigger than a phone?
questions.explanation: Most tablets have no keyboard. You tap and swipe on the screen with your fingers.

questions.question: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explanation: A byte is a group of eight bits. One byte can hold a single letter, such as "A".

questions.question: Which computer, built by IBM, beat the chess champion Garry Kasparov in a match in 1997?
questions.explanation: Deep Blue could look at about 200 million chess positions every second. It was a landmark for artificial intelligence.

questions.question: What does the Turing test try to find out?
questions.correct: If a machine can pass for a human
wrong: How fast a computer can work
If a file has a computer virus
How many bits a file holds
questions.explanation: Alan Turing suggested it in 1950. If a person cannot tell whether they are talking to a machine, the machine passes.

questions.question: Tim Berners-Lee invented the web while working at which European research centre?
questions.explanation: CERN is near Geneva in Switzerland. Scientists there needed an easy way to share papers between computers.

questions.question: What do the letters in "USB" stand for?
questions.explanation: USB was made in the 1990s so that one type of plug could connect many kinds of devices.

questions.question: What does "HTML" stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML is the code that tells a browser the structure of a web page: headings, paragraphs, links and pictures.

questions.question: In a web address that starts with "https", what does the "s" stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts the data between you and the website. That makes it hard for others to read it on the way.

questions.question: Nokia, the company famous for its mobile phones, was founded in which country?
questions.explanation: Nokia began as a paper mill in 1865 and is named after a town in Finland. Its phones were very popular in the 1990s and early 2000s.

questions.question: What is a CAPTCHA test on a website made to tell apart?
questions.explanation: Reading twisted letters or picking pictures is easy for people but was hard for programs that try to fill in forms.

questions.question: Which language is mainly used to set the colours, fonts and layout of web pages?
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets. HTML gives a page its content, and CSS makes it look good.

questions.question: Which part of a computer is its short-term working memory?
questions.explanation: RAM holds the programs and files you are using right now. It is emptied when the computer is switched off.

questions.question: What does the SIM card in a mobile phone do?
questions.explanation: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module. You can move it to another phone to keep your number.

questions.question: In which decade was the first text message (SMS) sent?
questions.explanation: It was sent in December 1992 and said "Merry Christmas". It was sent to a phone, from a computer.

questions.question: Which early computer network, started in the USA in 1969, grew into the internet?
questions.explanation: ARPANET first linked four computers at universities and research centres. Later networks joined it, and together they became the internet.

questions.question: What do the letters "CPU" stand for?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the part that runs the instructions. Phones also have a CPU, but a very small one.

questions.question: What do the letters "IP" stand for in "IP address"?
questions.explanation: An IP address is like a postal address for a device. It lets data find its way across the internet.

questions.question: Which programming language is named after a British comedy group?
questions.explanation: Its creator was a fan of Monty Python. The name has nothing to do with the snake, even if the logo has one.

questions.question: What does "open source" mean for a piece of software?
questions.correct: Anyone can read and change its code
wrong: It is free for one day
questions.explanation: Open-source programs, such as Linux, are built by people who share and improve the code together.

questions.question: What does a firewall do?
questions.explanation: A firewall checks the data going in and out and stops what is not allowed, like a guard at a gate.

questions.question: Which Finnish student started writing the Linux system in 1991?
questions.explanation: He first shared it as a hobby project. Linux went on to run many servers, phones and supercomputers.

questions.question: What was Colossus, built in Britain during the Second World War, used for?
questions.explanation: Colossus was one of the first electronic computers. It helped read German messages and was kept secret for years.

questions.question: What does the word "bit" come from?
questions.explanation: A bit is a single 0 or 1. The word was made popular by the scientist Claude Shannon.

questions.question: What is "phishing"?
questions.explanation: A phishing message may look like it comes from your bank. Never type passwords after clicking a link you don't trust.

questions.question: What is encryption used for?
questions.correct: Scrambling data so others can't read it
questions.explanation: Messages and online shopping use encryption. Without the secret key, the data looks like nonsense.

questions.question: Which kind of computer drive has no moving parts inside?
questions.explanation: An SSD stores data in chips. It is quiet and fast, while a hard disk has spinning plates.

questions.question: A phone finds its position with GPS by using signals from what?
questions.explanation: GPS satellites circle the Earth and send out the time. The phone uses the signals to work out where it is.

questions.question: What is a "cookie" on a website?
questions.correct: A small file saved by your browser
wrong: A picture on the home page
questions.explanation: Cookies can remember what is in your basket or which language you chose.

questions.question: What is a "cell" in a spreadsheet?
questions.correct: The box where a row and a column meet
questions.explanation: Each cell has a name, such as B3, made from its column letter and row number.

questions.question: In programming, what is a "loop"?
wrong: A way to save a file
questions.explanation: With a loop, you don't have to write the same line a thousand times. You tell the computer to repeat it.

questions.question: What does "streaming" a film mean?
questions.correct: Watching it as it arrives online
questions.explanation: You don't need to wait for the whole file before it starts. Music, games and live TV can be streamed too.

questions.question: What do the letters "QR" in "QR code" stand for?
questions.explanation: A QR code is a square pattern that a phone camera reads very quickly. It can open a web page.

questions.question: The word "robot" comes from a Czech word meaning what?
questions.explanation: Writer Karel Čapek used it in a play in 1920. The Czech word "robota" means hard, forced work.

questions.question: What is "machine learning"?
wrong: A way of building faster chips
questions.explanation: Instead of being told every rule, the program learns from many examples, such as photos of cats.

questions.question: Why does a phone touchscreen react to your finger but not to a wooden pencil?
questions.explanation: Most screens notice the change in an electric field when a finger touches them. Special gloves have threads that conduct.

questions.question: Which of these is an operating system for computers?
questions.explanation: An operating system runs the computer and lets other programs work. Windows, macOS and Linux are well known.

questions.question: Bjarne Stroustrup, who created the programming language C++, comes from which country?
questions.explanation: He was born in Aarhus. He began work on C++ in 1979 at Bell Labs in the USA.

questions.question: Artificial neural networks are loosely inspired by which part of the body?
questions.explanation: They have many simple units joined in layers, like nerve cells. They are used to recognise speech and pictures.

questions.question: Which sensor in a phone notices when you turn it sideways?
questions.explanation: The accelerometer feels movement and tilt. That is how the screen knows to rotate.

questions.question: What is a hashtag (#) used for in messages and posts?
questions.correct: To mark a topic so people can find it
questions.explanation: Clicking a hashtag shows other posts that use the same one.

questions.question: What does "multitasking" mean for a computer?
questions.explanation: A processor can switch between tasks so fast that they seem to run at the same time. Chips with several cores really do run them together.

questions.question: In 1969, the first message sent over ARPANET was cut short when the system crashed. Which two letters arrived?
questions.explanation: The team meant to type "LOGIN". The system crashed after "LO", and they typed the rest later.

questions.question: Which computer pioneer wrote one of the first compilers in the early 1950s?
questions.explanation: Her A-0 system appeared in 1952. Her later language FLOW-MATIC was a model for COBOL.

questions.question: Moore's law says that the number of what on a chip roughly doubles every two years?
questions.explanation: Gordon Moore first wrote about the trend in 1965. For decades it helped computers become much faster and smaller.

questions.question: In a von Neumann computer, where are programs and data stored?
questions.explanation: This stored-program idea is used in most computers. It means a computer can load a new program as easily as new data.

questions.question: ENIAC, an early electronic computer of the 1940s, used thousands of which part to do its calculations?
questions.explanation: Vacuum tubes were glass tubes that acted as switches. ENIAC filled a large room and used a lot of power.

questions.question: The transistor was invented in 1947 at which laboratory?
questions.explanation: The transistor replaced the vacuum tube. It was smaller, cooler and used much less power.

questions.question: Which programming language did Dennis Ritchie develop in the early 1970s?
questions.explanation: C was used to write the Unix system. Many later languages, such as C++ and Java, borrow its style.

questions.question: The programming language COBOL was made mainly for which kind of work?
questions.explanation: COBOL is short for Common Business-Oriented Language. It was designed in 1959 to read almost like English.

questions.question: What does DNS do on the internet?
questions.explanation: It works like a phone book. You type a name, and DNS finds the number that computers use.

questions.question: What does the code "ASCII" give to each letter, digit and symbol?
questions.explanation: For example, the capital letter "A" has the number 65. Unicode later grew to cover letters from all languages.

questions.question: How many different values can eight bits hold?
questions.explanation: Each bit has two choices, and 2 multiplied by itself eight times is 256. That is why colour values often go from 0 to 255.

questions.question: How many different symbols does the hexadecimal number system use?
questions.explanation: Hex uses the digits 0 to 9 and the letters A to F. Programmers like it because it is a short way to write binary.

questions.question: In 1936, Alan Turing described an imaginary machine. What was it used to study?
questions.correct: What can and cannot be computed
questions.explanation: The idea showed what any computer could do in theory. It became one of the foundations of computer science.

questions.question: RFID tags, such as those in some travel cards, are read using what?
questions.explanation: The reader sends a radio signal. The tag uses its energy to send back a short code.

questions.question: In a network, what does a "ping" measure?
questions.correct: The round-trip time of a signal
wrong: How much data a file holds
questions.explanation: A low ping means a fast response. It matters a lot in online games and video calls.

questions.question: A GPS receiver needs signals from at least how many satellites to find its position and the time?
questions.explanation: With a perfect clock, three would be enough. The fourth lets the receiver correct its own, less exact clock.

questions.question: Which engineer chose the "@" sign for email addresses in 1971?
questions.explanation: He used "@" to separate the user's name from the computer's name. He also sent one of the first networked emails.

questions.question: Which pair of rules, designed by Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn in the 1970s, is the basis of the internet?
questions.explanation: TCP/IP breaks data into small packets and sends them across the network. They are put back together at the end.

questions.question: Konrad Zuse built the Z3, one of the first working programmable computers, in 1941. Which country was he from?
questions.explanation: He built his first computer, the Z1, in his parents' flat in Berlin. The Z3 was destroyed in a bombing raid in 1943.

questions.question: The term "artificial intelligence" was coined for a 1956 summer workshop. At which college was it held?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy chose the term. The group hoped to make machines that could use language and learn, but it took much longer than they expected.

questions.question: Many self-driving cars use LiDAR to see their surroundings. What does LiDAR use?
questions.explanation: It measures how long the light takes to bounce back. From this a computer builds a 3D map of the road.

questions.question: In Isaac Asimov's stories, what does the First Law of Robotics say a robot may not do?
questions.explanation: Asimov invented his Three Laws in the 1940s. His stories are about how the rules can go wrong.

questions.question: The Y2K problem came from computers that stored the year with only how many digits?
questions.explanation: A year stored as "99" could turn into "00" in the year 2000. Computers could then think it was 1900.

questions.question: What does a compiler do?
wrong: Runs code one line at a time
Finds and fixes bugs in code
Makes files smaller to save space
questions.explanation: People write code in a language like C. The compiler turns it into machine code for the chip.

questions.question: In the phone standard GSM, launched in Europe in the early 1990s, what does the "M" stand for?
questions.explanation: GSM stands for Global System for Mobile communications. It made it possible to use one phone in many countries.

questions.question: A CD stores music as tiny pits that are read by what?
questions.explanation: The laser shines on the spinning disc. The pits and flat parts reflect the light differently.

questions.question: QR codes were invented in the 1990s to keep track of what?
questions.explanation: A Japanese company made them for car factories. A QR code holds much more data than an ordinary barcode.

questions.question: In 1947, engineers found a real insect causing a fault in the Harvard Mark II computer. What was it?
questions.explanation: It was stuck in a relay, and the team taped it into the log book as a joke. Engineers had called faults "bugs" long before that.

questions.question: In digital logic, when does an AND gate give an output of 1?
questions.explanation: AND, OR and NOT gates are the building blocks of chips. A processor is made from huge numbers of them.

questions.question: How many bits are there in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: 32 bits allow about 4 billion addresses. IPv6 uses 128 bits because we ran short.

questions.question: What does a servo motor in a robot arm do well?
questions.explanation: A servo has a small controller that checks its position. That is how a robot arm can reach exact points.

questions.question: What is a computer "worm"?
questions.correct: A program that copies itself on networks
wrong: A scratch on a hard disk
A cable that links two computers
questions.explanation: Unlike many viruses, a worm does not need a host file. It copies itself from computer to computer.

questions.question: The first prototype of the computer mouse in the 1960s had a case made of what?
questions.explanation: Douglas Engelbart's team carved a wooden shell for it. It had two wheels, not a ball.

questions.question: The small, cheap Raspberry Pi computer for learning to code comes from which country?
questions.explanation: It was created by a charity in Cambridge, England. The first model came out in 2012.

questions.question: What does "NFC", used for tapping a phone to pay, stand for?
questions.explanation: NFC only works over a few centimetres. The short range helps to keep payments safe.

questions.question: The first web page, made at CERN, was about what?
questions.explanation: It was on the first website, info.cern.ch. It explained what the World Wide Web was and how to set up a web server.

questions.question: In which year did CERN make the web's technology free for everyone to use?
questions.explanation: The decision let anyone build web software without paying. This helped the web to grow fast.

questions.question: A qubit is the basic unit of information in which kind of computer?
questions.explanation: A qubit can be in a mix of 0 and 1 at the same time. Quantum computers could solve certain problems much faster.

questions.question: What does a hash function do?
questions.correct: Turns data into a short fingerprint
questions.explanation: Even a tiny change to the data gives a completely different hash. Sites use hashes to protect stored passwords.

questions.question: Which early web browser from 1993 helped to make web pages with pictures popular?
questions.explanation: Mosaic could show pictures and text on the same page. Many later browsers grew from its ideas.
